search_space._comment_mode: 'mode' is itself an optimized hyperparameter: each trial samples whether to run 'rag' or 'agentic', then only that mode's sub-space below is sampled. Restrict choices to a single mode (e.g. ["rag"]) to optimize just that mode instead.
search_space._comment_rag: Full list of rag fields: k_standard, k_deep_dive, top_n, temperature, max_tokens, reranker_enabled, reranker_model, deep_dive, hyde_enabled, bm25_enabled, title_boost_enabled, k_retrieve, deep_dive_batch_size, expansion_char_budget. k_standard/k_deep_dive replace the single 'k' CLI override (chatbot.py --k still exists for a flat override, but isn't used here since only ONE of k_standard/k_deep_dive actually applies per trial anyway, picked by that trial's own deep_dive value — see chatbot/core/rag_chatbot.py). k_retrieve is ignored in deep dive mode; deep_dive_batch_size only applies when deep_dive is true — both are harmless, just inert, on trials where they don't apply (TPE learns this on its own). reranker_model only has an effect when reranker_enabled is true.
search_space._comment_agentic: Full list of agentic fields: temperature, max_tokens, max_steps (the CodeAgent step budget), max_chars_per_page.
search_space._comment_model: Optional, flat sub-space (sampled every trial regardless of mode — the answering LLM applies either way). Full fields: model, base_url, api_key. Only 'model' is shown here: base_url/api_key pick an entirely different provider/endpoint, and since they're sampled independently a naive search could pair a model name with the wrong endpoint's api_key. If you want to compare providers, either add base_url/api_key here too and keep 'model' consistent with each (e.g. one categorical value per (base_url, api_key, model) trio isn't directly expressible — safer to run separate studies per provider), or just pin base_url/api_key via fixed_params.model and only search 'model' (multiple model names on the SAME endpoint, the common case). Remove this whole 'model' key from search_space to skip it entirely and always use chatbot/config.json's llm block.
search_space._comment_extraction: Optional, flat sub-space (sampled every trial regardless of mode), shipped ABSENT here on purpose — unlike everything else in this file, get_or_build() has no way to know a value 'already matches' your current extraction/config.json build, so even a single-value combination forces one real corpus re-extraction (minutes, no early-exit) before the first trial can even start. See extraction_timeout_seconds below and the 'Extraction parameters' section of README.md before adding this back. To enable, add: "extraction": {"chunking.char_chunk_size": {"type": "int", "low": 700, "high": 1300}, "embedding.model": {"type": "categorical", "choices": ["all-MiniLM-L6-v2"]}}. Full fields: use_token_chunking, chunking.max_tokens, chunking.overlap_tokens, chunking.char_chunk_size, chunking.char_overlap, quality.min_score, quality.min_word_count, quality.substantial_word_count, embedding.model, embedding.type, embedding.base_url, embedding.api_key. Keep each field to 2-3 values once enabled.

_comment_fixed_params: Per-key (mode name, 'model', or 'extraction') hyperparameters passed to every trial but never sampled — e.g. fixed_params.model = {"base_url": "...", "api_key": "..."} to pin the endpoint while search_space.model only searches 'model' names on it. Must not overlap with the matching search_space entry.
_comment_n_trials: Number of configurations Optuna will try. With Bayesian optimization (TPE), 30-50 trials is usually enough to clearly beat random/grid search on a search space this size.
_comment_timeout_seconds: Optional wall-clock budget for the whole study (stops launching new trials once exceeded). null = no limit, only n_trials governs the budget.
_comment_questions_limit: Cap the number of dataset questions evaluated per trial. Useful to dry-run/debug the optimizer itself quickly; set to null to use the full 94-question dataset for real runs.
_comment_chatbot_timeout_seconds: Timeout in seconds for a single chatbot.py question call. null = no limit.
_comment_extraction_timeout_seconds: Timeout in seconds for building ONE extraction variant (search_space.extraction). null = no limit — a real corpus re-extraction can legitimately take several minutes, so only set this if you want a hard ceiling.
_comment_workers: Threads used to evaluate questions of a SINGLE trial in parallel (same idea as benchmark.py --workers; -1 uses all CPUs). Each unit here is a full chatbot.py subprocess that reloads its own models from scratch (the RAG reranker alone is ~2-4GB of RAM) -- unlike a lightweight thread, so a high value can exhaust RAM and make the run appear to hang (or get OOM-killed) rather than actually deadlocking. Keep this modest (2-4) unless you've confirmed the machine has enough RAM for that many concurrent model loads, and keep it at 1 if the LLM endpoint enforces rate limits. Multiplies with n_jobs below (n_jobs x workers concurrent chatbot calls at once), so raise them one at a time.
_comment_n_jobs: Number of trials Optuna runs concurrently. Keep at 1 unless your LLM/chatbot backend can comfortably absorb several simultaneous full dataset evaluations at once — this also multiplies concurrent extraction builds if two trials sample different never-before-seen extraction combos at once (safe: each combo is serialized by its own lock — see evaluator/base/extraction_cache.py — but that many parallel multi-minute builds add up).
_comment_dataset_shuffle_seed: dataset.json is grouped by module/topic, not shuffled, so evaluating only the first N questions of a pruned trial would be a biased, unrepresentative sample. The dataset is shuffled once with this seed and then reused in that same order for every trial, so pruning compares trials on equivalent partial samples. Set to null to keep the file's original order (not recommended if pruning is enabled).
_comment_storage: Optuna storage URL, e.g. 'sqlite:///studies/chatbot_hyperparameter_optimization.db'. Leave null to auto-generate a local SQLite file under evaluator/optimizer/studies/<study_name>.db. Re-running with the same study_name/storage resumes and adds trials to the same study instead of starting over — valuable since a full study can take hours.
_comment_pruning: A trial only becomes eligible for pruning after n_warmup_trials other trials have fully completed (so the pruner has something to compare against) AND after min_questions_before_pruning questions have been evaluated within that trial itself (so one unlucky early question can't kill an otherwise good config). From then on it is re-checked every interval_questions questions, and pruned only if its running average score falls below the given percentile of other trials at the same step — trials of both modes are compared together, which is exactly what lets a bad rag config lose out to a good agentic one (or vice versa). Set enabled to false to always run every trial through the full dataset. Note: pruning can only cut short the per-question evaluation loop — it cannot help during an extraction build (search_space.extraction), which has no early-exit.
_comment_final_validation: Each metric score is stochastic (LLM-graded), so the single best-value trial found during the search could just be lucky. After optimization, the top_k trials (ranked by Optuna's value, regardless of which mode they used) are each re-evaluated on the FULL dataset 'repeats' more times (no pruning) to report a mean +/- standard deviation per candidate and pick a genuinely robust winner rather than a noisy outlier.
_comment_plots: Saves 3 PNGs to graphs/<study_name>/ after the search (requires matplotlib, already a project dependency): 01_optimization_history (objective value per trial, green=accepted/red=refused, plus the running best-so-far curve), 02_param_importances (which parameters actually moved the score, via Optuna's fANOVA evaluator — needs at least 2 completed trials), 03_param_evolution (one small subplot per sampled parameter, value vs trial number, same green/red coloring — useful to see whether the search is converging on a region for a given knob or still spread out). Set enabled to false (or --no-plots) to skip.
